ex: The shah was the king of Iran.
We read about the old shahs of Persia in class.
The museum shows the shah's crown and jewels.
Which shah built this beautiful palace in Tehran?

smartphone.note: People often just say "phone": "Call me on my phone."

titan.note: Also "Titan": a giant god in Greek myths, and a moon of Saturn.

ex: We sang karaoke with friends until midnight.
Let's go to a karaoke bar on Friday.
She always sings the same song at karaoke.
Is there a karaoke night at this bar?
We bought premium tickets with better seats.
This store sells premium coffee from Colombia.
Premium members don't see any ads in the app.
Does the hotel have premium rooms with a view?
premium.note: As a noun, "premium" often means money you pay for insurance: "a monthly premium."

ex: Her son was diagnosed with autism last year.
Autism affects how people talk and make friends.
The school has a program for kids with autism.
Where can I learn more about autism in children?
He ordered a bourbon with ice at the bar.
Bourbon is a kind of American whiskey.
She added a little bourbon to the cake.
Can I get a glass of bourbon, please?
bourbon.note: Uncountable, but "a bourbon" means a glass of it.

mix.note: Most often "mix" is a verb: "Mix the flour and eggs." As a noun: "a mix of styles."

screening.note: Also a showing of a film: "a screening of the new movie."

ex: Oxygen and hydrogen are the elements in water.
Trust is an important element of any friendship.
Gold is a chemical element with the symbol Au.
What are the key elements of a good resume?

aquarium.note: An aquarium at home is also called a "fish tank".

mandate.note: Often a verb: "The law mandates seat belts" (= requires). Also an order: "a mask mandate."

ex: Algebra was my favorite subject in school.
Can you help me with my algebra homework?
Basic algebra is useful in everyday life.
We have an algebra test on Friday.

sarcasm.note: Uncountable: say "a lot of sarcasm", not "a sarcasm".

ex: The detective always carried a revolver in his coat.
A revolver usually holds six bullets.
He kept an old revolver in a locked drawer.
The police found a revolver in the car.
The biathlon mass start begins at two o'clock.
In a mass start, all the skiers start together.
She won a gold medal in the mass start.
Are you going to watch the mass start on TV?
mass start.note: A sports term: a race where all athletes start together.

ex: The lead manager is responsible for the whole project.
Our lead manager plans the work for the team.
Who is the lead manager on this deal?
The bank acted as lead manager for the bond sale.
lead manager.note: "Lead manager" means the main manager of a project or a deal.

ex: The flag captain commanded the admiral's ship.
In old navies, the flag captain worked closely with the admiral.
The flag captain stood next to the admiral on deck.
Who was the flag captain of this famous ship?
flag captain.note: A naval term: the captain of the ship that carries the admiral.

ex: Each key on the keyboard sends its own scan code.
The computer reads the scan code and shows a letter.
This program shows the scan code of every key you press.
What is the scan code for the Enter key?
scan code.note: A computer term: the code a keyboard sends when you press a key.

ex: A general admiral was the highest rank in some old navies.
The tsar made his brother general admiral of the fleet.
The general admiral controlled all the ships of the empire.
Was the general admiral higher than a normal admiral?
general admiral.note: A historical rank: the top admiral in some old navies.

ex: A rally raid can last for two weeks in the desert.
The trucks in this rally raid drive across sand and rocks.
He drives a car in a famous rally raid every year.
Would you like to watch the rally raid on TV?
rally raid.note: A long off-road car race, often across a desert.

ex: The delta operator shows the change between two values.
In this class, we use the delta operator for differences.
Write the delta operator with the Greek letter Δ.
Can you explain how the delta operator works?
delta operator.note: A math term: an operator for differences, written with the Greek letter Δ.

general field marshal.gram: a general field marshal · general field marshals
ex: A general field marshal was the top rank in the old army.
The empress made him a general field marshal after the war.
Only a few officers ever became general field marshal.
Is a general field marshal higher than a general?
general field marshal.note: A historical rank in old Russian and German armies; English usually says "field marshal".

ex: The vacuum meter shows the pressure inside the tank.
Check the vacuum meter before you start the pump.
Our lab bought a new digital vacuum meter.
Why is the vacuum meter showing zero?
vacuum meter.note: Also called a "vacuum gauge", which is more common.

ex: Black rot can destroy a whole crop of grapes.
Wet summers often bring black rot to the vineyard.
These black spots on the leaves are black rot.
How can I protect my cabbage from black rot?
black rot.note: A plant disease. Uncountable: "The vines have black rot."

ex: The null vector has a length of zero.
Adding the null vector does not change a vector.
In this problem, the answer is the null vector.
Can a null vector have a direction?
The fascists took power in Italy in the 1920s.
He was called a fascist by his political enemies.
The fascists closed all the free newspapers.
My grandfather fought against the fascists in the war.
fascist.note: Also an adjective: "a fascist government." Often an insult for a very strict person.

ex: We pay for website hosting every year.
This company offers cheap hosting for small websites.
Our hosting provider had problems this morning.
Which hosting do you use for your online store?
hosting.note: Uncountable. Also a form of "host": "She is hosting a party tonight."

ex: He ordered a dry martini with an olive.
She drank a martini at the hotel bar.
Can we have two martinis, please?
This martini is too strong for me.
martini.note: Usually a cocktail of gin or vodka and vermouth, often with an olive.

beta.note: Also the Greek letter β. "In beta" means a program is still being tested.

ex: Children learn the alphabet in kindergarten.
The English alphabet has twenty-six letters.
Can you say the alphabet backward?
The Ukrainian alphabet has thirty-three letters.
Opium is made from a kind of poppy.
In the past, doctors used opium for pain.
The police found opium hidden in the truck.
Opium is illegal in most countries today.
My son reads manga every night before bed.
This manga was made into a TV show.
She draws her own manga in a notebook.
Where can I find the manga section in this store?
manga.note: Plural is usually also "manga": "I have ten manga."

ex: The doctor gave him an antidote to the poison.
There is no antidote for this snake bite.
Does the hospital have an antidote for this poison?
They found the antidote just in time.
antidote.note: Use "to" or "for": "an antidote to the poison".

ex: He gave her a bouquet of roses.
At the wedding, the bride threw her bouquet.
A bouquet of flowers stood on the table.
Can I order a bouquet for my mom's birthday?

cylinder.note: Also a part of a car engine, and a metal tank: "a gas cylinder".

ex: He studied Latin for two years in school.
Many English words come from Latin.
Nobody speaks Latin as a first language today.
What does this phrase in Latin mean?
Latin.note: Most often "Latin" is an adjective about Latin America: "Latin music", "Latin dance".

ex: The oil lobby is very powerful in the capital.
A strong farm lobby fought against the new law.
The gun lobby spent millions on the election campaign.
Environmental lobbies want stricter rules for factories.
lobby.note: Most often "lobby" means an entrance hall: "Meet me in the hotel lobby."

padre.note: Informal: a priest, often an army chaplain. The usual word is "priest".

boxer.note: Also a dog breed. "Boxers" or "boxer shorts" are men's underwear.

ex: The earthquake caused a huge tsunami.
A tsunami warning was issued for the coast.
The tsunami destroyed many homes near the beach.
What should we do if there is a tsunami?
